glosses: to condense (to decrease size or volume)
конденсация
конденсировать
kondensować
Condenser.

examples.text: In einem weiteren Wärmetauscher, dem so genannten Verflüssiger, wird das unter hohem Druck stehende, heiße Kältemittelgas nun kondensiert, wobei es seine Wärme wieder abgibt.
examples.translation: Dans un autre échangeur de chaleur, appelé condenseur, le gaz réfrigérant chaud et sous haute pression est alors condensé, ce qui lui permet de restituer sa chaleur.

glosses: vom Aggregatzustand gasförmig nach flüssig übergehen

examples.text: Die Luftfeuchtigkeit im Badezimmer kondensierte am Spiegel und bildete dort kleine Wassertröpfchen.
Wenn das von der baumreichen Vegetation ausgedünstete Wasser kondensiert, schrumpft das Volumen der lokalen Luftmasse, der Druck sinkt, und es entsteht ein Tief.

glosses: gasförmige Stoffe durch Druck oder Abkühlung verflüssigen

examples.text: Gase wie O₂, N₂, H₂, lassen sich auf Flächen kondensieren, welche mit flüssigem Helium gekühlt werden und Temperaturen von T ≈ 10K erreichen (…).
Gemäß der gestrichelten Linie in Abb. 1-1-28 ist es möglich, ein Gemisch durch Drucksenkung bei konstanter Temperatur zunächst teilweise zu kondensieren und dann wieder zu verdampfen.

glosses: etwas (zumeist Lebensmittel) durch Verdampfen eindicken

examples.text: Aufgrund des niedrigen Siedepunkts von Alkohol verdampft dieser beim Erwärmen und kondensiert.
Amalgame lassen sich im plastischen Zustand so kondensieren, dass auch schwierig zugängliche, approximale Kastenböden randständig gefüllt werden können.

translations.source_sense_description: intransitiv, Hilfsverb haben oder sein, Physik: vom Aggregatzustand gasförmig nach flüssig übergehen

glosses: To concentrate toward the essence by making more close, compact, or dense, thereby decreasing size or volume.

examples.text: An abridged dictionary can be further condensed to pocket size.
Boiling off water condenses a thin sauce into a soupier mixture.

In what shape they choose,
 Dilated or condensed, bright or obscure.
The secret course pursued both at Brussels and at Madrid may be condensed into the usual formula, dissimulation, procrastination, and again dissimulation.

glosses: To transform from a gaseous state into a liquid state via condensation.
To be transformed from a gaseous state into a liquid state.

examples.text: Water condenses on the window on cold days because of the warm air inside.

glosses: Condensed; compact; dense.

examples.text: The huge condense bodies of planets.

translations.source_sense_description: intransitiv, Hilfsverb haben oder sein, Physik: vom Aggregatzustand gasförmig nach flüssig übergehen

glosses: To make something happen suddenly and quickly.

examples.text: to precipitate a journey, or a conflict
it precipitated their success
if they be stout and daring, it may precipitate their designs, and prove dangerous
Back to his sight precipitates her steps.
Freshly arrived in Paris in 1871 at the age of 17, Rimbaud proceded ^([sic]) to precipitate the collapse of Verlaine's marital menage, and with it his social position.

glosses: To throw an object or person from a great height.

examples.text: In gallopping heedlessly along, with her eyes turned upwards, she had unwarily approached too near the bank; it had given way with her, and she and her horse had been precipitated to the pebbled margin of the river.

glosses: To send violently into a certain state or condition.

examples.text: we were precipitated into a conflict

glosses: (chemistry) To come out of a liquid solution into solid form.

examples.text: Adding the acid will cause the salt to precipitate.

glosses: (chemistry) To separate a substance out of a liquid solution into solid form.
To have water in the air fall to the ground, for example as rain, snow, sleet, or hail; be deposited as condensed droplets.

examples.text: It will precipitate tomorrow, but we don't know whether as rain or snow.

glosses: To cause (water in the air) to condense or fall to the ground.

examples.text: The light vapour of the preceding evening had been precipitated by the cold.

glosses: To fall headlong.
To act too hastily; to be precipitous.
headlong; falling steeply or vertically.

examples.text: When the full stores their ancient bounds disdain, / Precipitate the furious torrent flows.

glosses: Very steep; precipitous.
With a hasty impulse; hurried; headstrong.

examples.text: Though thoughtful far beyond your years, you are very inexperienced; and I would not have a preference that may originate in your little knowledge of others, or a romantic exaggeration of slight kindnesses, lead you into a precipitate union with me, unless you most seriously examine your own heart, and weigh the various consequences.

glosses: Moving with excessive speed or haste; overly hasty.

examples.text: The king was too precipitate in declaring war.
a precipitate case of disease
Being a trifle precipitate in his entry, he trod on a bottle, and was instantly extinguished by a Japanese screen, which appeared to collapse on him out of pure decrepitude.
'One moment!" said Malone. "I beg, sir, that you will not be precipitate. I value your friendship too much to risk the loss of it if it can, in any way, be avoided."

glosses: Performed very rapidly or abruptly.

examples.text: It had cost me a distinct psychological effort to do so, and now that I was shut inside I had a momentary longing for precipitate retreat.

glosses: A product resulting from a process, event, or course of action.

examples.text: As for the musculature it is a precipitate of Spirit and the signature of the cosmos is in it.

glosses: A solid that exits the liquid phase of a solution.

translations.source_sense_description: intransitiv, Hilfsverb haben oder sein, Physik: vom Aggregatzustand gasförmig nach flüssig übergehen

glosses: Resserrer dans un moindre espace, réduire.

examples.text: Le froid condense les corps.
Quand je vais camper, je prends avec moi du lait condensé pour le café.

glosses: Faire passer (ou passer, pronominal) de l'état gazeux à l'état liquide ou solide, « matière condensée ».

examples.text: La pelouse était couverte de faibles vapeurs condensées, qui déroulaient leurs blancs flocons sur la pointe des herbes.
Dans l’air rafraîchi où une impalpable brume se condensait en rosée, les bêtes levèrent leur mufle humide […].

glosses: Lier des molécules (ou se lier, pronominal) par réaction chimique par une réaction de condensation.

examples.text: Concernant le mécanisme réactionnel, les groupes alkoxysilyle s'hydrolysent et les groupes silanol formés se condensent entre eux. Un polysiloxane est obtenu.

glosses: Resserrer, résumer, compacter un discours un raisonnement.

examples.text: Condenser sa pensée, l’exprimer en peu de mots.
